newsitem.title: USA: Online ad revenues hit record $129.5 million in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Online ad revenues hit record $129.5 million in Q1.

text.p: Online ad revenues surged to $129.5 million in the first quarter, a rise of more than $20 million, or 18 percent, from record fourth quarter 1996 levels, the Internet Advertising Bureau reported.
Total advertising spending in the first quarter rose 333 percent from year-ago levels of just under $30 million.
The IAB's survey found that online advertising revenue is being spread more evenly across the top 50 online publishers.
For example, in the first quarter the top 10 publishers online accounted for 63 percent of advertising revenues, compared with 75 percent one year ago.

"Media spending is traditionally soft in the first quarter, so these are particularly significant results," said Rich LeFurgy, IAB chairman and senior vice president of advertising at ESPN/ABC Internet Ventures. "Acceptance of the medium is clearly growing among advertisers and more and more publishers now view advertising as the revenue model of choice."

The survey, which represents data from more than 200 Internet publishers representing more than 86 percent of industry revenues, found 45 percent of respondents forecast 1997 revenues will fall between $500 million and $600 million, with 17 percent forecasting more than $700 million.

Online advertising revenues for 1996 were $267 million, of which $109.5 was recorded in the fourth quarter, according to the IAB, whose "Advertising Revenue Reporting Program" is compiled by Coopers & Lybrand LLP's New Media Group.

Five leading industry categories dominated Internet advertising spending in the first quarter. Computing products accounted for 30 percent, telecommunications for 22 percent, consumer-related businesses for 17 percent, financial services for 11 percent and new media businesses for 10 percent.
Telecommunications industry spending increased 13 percent in the first quarter and the financial services industry joined the top five online spenders for the first time, IAB said.
The survey foundthe vast majority of revenue transactions continue to be cash-based, with barter deals accounting for only three percent of total spending.

Banner advertising -- in which advertisements are depicted as a band across a Web page, continues to dominate online spending at 70 percent, although a full 24 percent of online ad dollars was dedicated to sponsorship of online content.

Asked to identify the key obstacle to online advertising growth, 31 percent cited accurate audience measurement and another 31 percent said the need for a greater audience base, while only 10 percent pointed to need for higher bandwidth.
